mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the FEDFUNDS rate increases by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within two months indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE rises by more than 0.5% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the broader economy benefits from increased construction activity and related sectors.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods where HOUST shows a sustained increase over three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within a quarter indicates supply chain disruptions or a slowing economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies face production challenges and reduced output.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where INDPRO drops by more than 2% within a quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 jobs in a month, it signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 jobs in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals increased consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies benefit from higher sales and increased profitability.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS increases by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded and the Fed may tighten monetary policy further.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS is above 2% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.3% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and real GDP (GDPC1) both show a quarter-over-quarter increase of more than 1%, it signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and economic growth prospects improve.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and GDPC1 both increase > 1% quarter-over-quarter
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where both INDPRO and GDPC1 increase by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter.
